summary: A 1856 brick tower on the clay cliffs at Martha's Vineyard's western tip, site of the 1884 City of Columbus rescue and moved inland in 2015.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster is from the USLHS archive (NARA registers). Disagreements stated in the story: first-lighting date (18 vs 7 Nov 1799), original appropriation ($5,750 vs $570), tower date (1854 vs 1856), keeper's house replacement (1902 vs 1906), automation (1956 vs 1960 vs lens removal 1952 vs 1961), move distance (175 vs 134 ft), wreck date (LighthouseFriends 19 Jan 1884 vs newspaper sequence implying 17-18 Jan; the newspaper does not itself give the date of the wreck). The role of keeper Pease in launching the lifeboat is not established by the newspaper pages read (LighthouseFriends says the keepers gathered the crew; the Coast Guard Museum says the white keeper led); the story does not state it. The Dukes County Intelligencer and Massachusetts Humane Society reports were not consulted and would add detail on the 1884 rescue. Newspaper OCR spelling of 'Indians' phrases kept in evidence quotes only. The 1900 Light-House Board report (stairs) and 1901 report entry for Gay Head were seen but not used. Gay Head Life-Saving Station has its own record (us-ma-gay-head-life-saving-station). The lighthouse is owned by the Town of Aquinnah; tours are announced on gayheadlight.org, whose operator is not stated on the page read. Whether the tower can be climbed on current tours is not stated. Fact-check 2026-10-27: newspaper 'Horatio M. Pease' vs archive/LighthouseFriends 'Horatio N.'; story keeps the paper's spelling. The date on which Gay Head was first reached by correspondents is not given in the 21 Jan page read, so the story gives none. Tower height 51 ft (NRHP, LHF) vs 52 ft (history page) stated. Keeper's house razing: 1956 (history page) vs 1961 (NRHP) stated.
